figures.Fig13.1: Particles are in random motion. Original figure archived as c12-phy-ch13-fig-brownian (drawn for this lesson; not the textbook's picture).

findings: The book gives the year of Brown's observation as 1927; it was 1827. Its definition ('random motion of molecules in a gas') is clarified: Brownian motion is the motion of suspended particles driven by molecular collisions. Both corrected in a warning.
The book's statements that particle size and viscosity are 'inversely proportional' to speed are given qualitatively.

Owner rule (2026-10-21): the English lesson carries only the book's content. Our explanations, notes on the print, self-check questions with their answers, the recap, 3D models and figures the book does not print are in the Roman Urdu lesson only; where the book's own Quick Check or Brain Teaser questions are given, the English lesson lists them without answers.
